implementation: select_native_worker_io chooses seven existing concrete SDK adapters using native defaults. It validates all function pointers and refuses occupied target slots before constructing adapters.

All seven adapter owners are constructed before committing any target. Server and Runtime share exactly the same socket and dispatcher objects; IOC constructor/gates/accept/factory/cancel are installed in their actual owning slots.

Selection preserves LastError. SDK-table functions are not invoked during selection; only LastError bookkeeping calls are made. No socket, IOCP, accept, wait, WSAStartup or extra worker starts in this function.

The existing owning Runtime/three-worker scenario now calls this selector from the original worker configure callback. Custom coarse socket/dispatcher test classes were replaced by SDK shims around the same concrete classes used by native defaults.

The source scenario checks empty targets after failed import validation, paired identities/native classes, LastError, refusal to replace occupied providers and absence of fabricated lifecycle/cancellation/executor/TLS/drain providers.
